title: One syllable, four meanings: Mandarin tones

publish.title: One syllable, four meanings: the Mandarin tones
publish.description: The four tones of Mandarin with the classic ma example.

scenes.headline: One syllable can mean four different things
scenes.narration: In Mandarin, the same sound can mean four different things. The difference is the tone.

scenes.headline: The four tones
scenes.narration: The first tone is high and level, mother. The second rises, hemp. The third dips, horse. The fourth falls sharply, to scold.

scenes.headline: A fifth, neutral tone
scenes.narration: There is also a light, neutral tone on some syllables. Pitch changes the word, so tones matter as much as vowels.

scenes.headline: Listen first, then say it aloud
scenes.narration: Practise by listening and repeating, and record yourself. Tones are easier to hear than to describe.

scenes.headline: Say them aloud
scenes.narration: Say the four words in a row, and listen to the pitch.
